He controlled many Al Badr camps
2014-09-11T00:00:45+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/he-controlled-many-al-badr-camps-41201

Jamaat-e-Islami leader Muhammad Kamaruzzaman was a very influential Al Badr leader controlling all the Al Badr camps in Mymensingh, Sherpur and Nalitabari in 1971, Attorney General Mahbubey Alam told the Supreme Court yesterday. He was citing a statement made before International Crimes Tribunal (ICT)-2 by a prosecution witness, Monowar Hossain Khan alias Mohan Munshi, who was a guard of an Al Badr camp in Mymensingh during the 1971 Liberation War. Mahbubey was placing arguments on the 14th day of hearing on Kamaruzzaman's appeal challenging his death sentence for crimes against humanity committed in 1971. Mohan Munshi is “a star witness” as he admitted to the ICT-2 that he was an Al Badr member and Kamaruzzaman was his boss. Mahbubey also turned down objections of defence counsels on charges of Kamaruzzaman killing one Badiuzzaman of Ramnagar village in Jhenaigati of Sherpur and torturing Syed Abdul Hannan, the then principal of Sherpur College. A four-member Appellate Division bench headed by Justice Surendra Kumar Sinha is expected to resume the hearing next week. ICT-2 sentenced to death Kamaruzzaman on May 9 last year. He filed the appeal with the SC on June 6 last year.
